chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Rashid, from his father who said:
I saw Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and upon him was a black cloak and a blue pallium.

key_terms.دُرَّاعَة: A type of long outer garment or cloak worn over other clothes
key_terms.طَيْلَسَان: A pallium or draped shawl, worn by scholars and religious figures; of Persian origin

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Zayn al-Abidin wear black clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith records a direct eyewitness account of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, the fourth Imam, d. 95 AH) dressed in a black cloak (durra'a) and a blue pallium (taylasan). The narration appears in the chapter on wearing black clothing, serving as evidence that the Imam himself wore black garments. The taylasan was a distinctive draped outer wrap, often associated with scholars and men of religious stature in early Islamic society.
